name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R382 in the DNA-binding domain contacts the DNA phosphate backbone, and Arg-to-Trp removes that positive charge and adds a bulky hydrophobic side chain, so STAT3 binds its response element less well.", "mechanism_class": "nucleic_acid_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E3", "E12", "E4"], "would_refute": "The R382 side chain in DNA-bound structures (for example 6QHD) lies more than about 5 \u00c5 from every DNA atom, and its substitution in a model of the DNA complex creates no steric or electrostatic clash with the DNA.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Only the direct evidence about this substitution points here: UniProt E2 reports reduced DNA-binding ability for R382W, and E3 places residue 382 in the STAT DNA-binding domain. E12 is a DNA-complex structure that observes residue 382. Missing: no structure shows R382 contacting DNA directly (G2), and no assay tests R382W binding (G1)."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R382 packs into or stabilises the DNA-binding domain fold, and the bulky Trp side chain destabilises the domain so that less folded, functional STAT3 is available.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E4", "E5", "E6", "E18"], "would_refute": "Predicted \u0394\u0394G for R382W (for example with FoldX or Rosetta on the AlphaFold model and on 6QHD) is near zero or stabilising, and R382 side-chain burial is low in all experimental structures, so no packing defect is predicted.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Conservation (E5), popEVE (E6), EVE (E7) and AlphaMissense (E4) all predict damage, but these tools score deleteriousness and do not separate fold destabilisation from loss of DNA contact. The record has no stability measurement and no protein-level data for R382W (G4), and the only haploinsufficiency evidence (E13) concerns a nonsense variant. So this ranks below the binding-specific hypothesis."}
